title: Introduction to remart
text: getBM() accepts familiar attributes, filters, values arguments. following query retrieves basic annotations two human Ensembl genes. connection Ensembl handled internally, mart object required. Attributes returned order requested. Duplicate identifiers handled internally, identifiers Ensembl find omitted warning.
code: gene_ids <- c("ENSG00000157764", "ENSG00000004939")  gene_annotations <- getBM(   attributes = c(     "ensembl_gene_id",     "external_gene_name",     "chromosome_name",     "start_position",     "end_position"   ),   filters = "ensembl_gene_id",   values = gene_ids )  head(gene_annotations)

title: Introduction to remart
text: Transcript-level attributes can requested using gene identifiers. gene can multiple transcripts, may return multiple rows one gene. Alternatively, transcript identifiers can used filter query transcript-oriented:
code: transcript_annotations <- getBM(   attributes = c(     "ensembl_gene_id",     "ensembl_transcript_id",     "ensembl_peptide_id",     "transcript_biotype"   ),   filters = "ensembl_gene_id",   values = "ENSG00000157764" )  head(transcript_annotations) getBM(   attributes = c(     "ensembl_transcript_id",     "ensembl_gene_id",     "ensembl_peptide_id"   ),   filters = "ensembl_transcript_id",   values = "ENST00000357654" )

title: Introduction to remart
text: workflows written around biomaRt::getGene(), getGene() provides convenient gene-level interface: returned columns include ensembl_gene_id, hgnc_symbol, genomic coordinates, strand, description. Ensembl’s REST response provide band field used biomaRt, remart returns band NA warning.
code: getGene(   id = c("ENSG00000157764", "ENSG00000004939"),   type = "ensembl_gene_id" )

title: Introduction to remart
text: getSequence() retrieves sequences Ensembl gene, transcript, peptide identifier. example, cDNA sequence can retrieved transcript follows: Upstream downstream bases can requested supported sequence queries: Coordinate-based requests using chromosome, start, end yet implemented.
code: cdna <- getSequence(   seqType = "cdna",   type = "ensembl_transcript_id",   id = "ENST00000357654" )  summary(cdna) extended_cdna <- getSequence(   seqType = "cdna",   type = "ensembl_transcript_id",   id = "ENST00000357654",   upstream = 100,   downstream = 100 )  summary(extended_cdna)

title: Introduction to remart

title: Introduction to remart
text: typical biomaRt workflow creates connection calling getBM(): remart, connection setup removed query can usually adapted directly: Several obsolete connection-related arguments accepted ... source compatibility. Check listAttributes() function reference migrating workflow uses less common filters attributes.
code: # A biomaRt workflow. # This example is not actually run as the biomart service is unstable. gene_ids <- c("ENSG00000157764", "ENSG00000004939") attrs <- c(   "ensembl_gene_id",   "external_gene_name",   "chromosome_name",   "start_position",   "end_position" ) mart <- biomaRt::useEnsembl("ensembl", dataset = "hsapiens_gene_ensembl") biomaRt::getBM(   attributes = attrs,   filters = "ensembl_gene_id",   values = gene_ids,   mart = mart ) gene_ids <- c("ENSG00000157764", "ENSG00000004939") attrs <- c(   "ensembl_gene_id",   "external_gene_name",   "chromosome_name",   "start_position",   "end_position" ) getBM(   attributes = attrs,   filters = "ensembl_gene_id",   values = gene_ids )
